key_insight: The paper reconstructs high-fidelity 3D turbulent flow fields from coarse data by combining multiscale volumetric learning, temporal state-space modeling, and physics-based regularization.
engineering_relevance: This enables more accurate and cost-effective surrogate modeling for CFD, flow monitoring, and atmospheric analysis when direct high-resolution simulation or measurement is impractical.
method: Multiscale neural operator recovers fine 3D spatial structures from coarse inputs.
State space model enforces coherent time evolution in reconstructed turbulence.
Navier-Stokes residuals and a mixture-of-experts module add physical plausibility and adapt to unknown coarse-graining.
evidence_signal: The framework is evaluated on canonical turbulent systems and atmospheric reanalysis data, where it reduces reconstruction error and better preserves multiscale structure and temporal coherence than learning-based and classical baselines.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the physics residuals, temporal model, and expert routing generalize to new flow regimes, noise levels, or coarse-graining patterns.
paper_title: High-fidelity Three-Dimensional Flow Field Reconstruction Driven by Turbulent Fluid Dynamics
